figures.caption: 圖：商場裡的盲盒販售機
figures.description: 商場角落有一台透明的盲盒販售機，機身的海報印著一整套十二款的小動物公仔，其中一款「隱藏版」只畫了一個大問號。一名男學生站在機器前，盯著剛拆開的公仔，一臉失望；他腳邊已經散落七、八個拆開的空盒。他身旁的女生正拿手機掃碼，準備再買一盒。旁邊的長椅上，兩個女生開心地交換彼此重複抽到的公仔。

questions.stem: 提示：盲盒在打開之前看不到裡面是哪一款公仔，這種「抽抽看」的樂趣吸引了許多年輕人，有人甚至一次花掉好幾週的零用錢。請根據下圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖中的情景；第二段說明盲盒為什麼這麼受年輕人歡迎，以及購買盲盒可能帶來的影響。

1.explanation_zh: 第一段描述圖中的情景；第二段有兩個任務：盲盒受歡迎的原因，以及購買盲盒可能帶來的影響。原因不要只寫「很可愛」，可以從驚喜感、收集心理、社群分享來寫；影響可以是金錢、環境或人際，好處與壞處都可以寫，但要具體。
evidence: 第二段說明盲盒為什麼這麼受年輕人歡迎
購買盲盒可能帶來的影響
1.strategy_zh: 圖中的空盒可以帶出「浪費」，交換公仔的兩人可以帶出「交友」，失望的男生可以帶出「花費失控」，三者都是影響的線索。
hints: 第一段：先寫販售機，再寫機器前的兩個人，最後寫長椅上的兩人
第二段前半：兩個原因，其中一個用自己或朋友的經驗說明
第二段後半：至少一項影響，最後提出一個具體做法（例如設定預算）

content.focus_zh: 第一段要寫出販售機、隱藏版、失望的男生與空盒、準備再買的女生、交換公仔的兩人；第二段要有至少兩個受歡迎的原因（驚喜感、收集成套、社群炫耀等）與至少一項影響（金錢、垃圾、交友），最好有自己或朋友的具體經驗或金額。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。

空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The picture shows a group of teenagers at a blind box machine in a shopping mall. A poster on the machine shows a set of twelve small animal figures, and one of them is a secret figure with a question mark. A boy in front of the machine has just opened a box, but he looks disappointed. There are already seven or eight empty boxes around his feet. Next to him, a girl is holding her phone and getting ready to buy one more. Meanwhile, two girls on a bench are happily trading extra figures with each other.
Blind boxes are popular among young people for several reasons. First, the surprise of not knowing what is inside is exciting. Second, many students want to collect a whole set, especially the secret figure. I understand this feeling well. For example, I once spent a whole week’s pocket money on five boxes, but I still did not get the panda I wanted. However, buying blind boxes can have bad effects. Because each box costs about three hundred dollars, students can easily spend too much money. Also, the empty boxes and plastic bags create a lot of waste. In my opinion, blind boxes can be fun, but students should set a budget before they buy. In short, a small surprise should not turn into a big problem.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 描述涵蓋圖中三組人物，原因與影響都有、並有自己的花費經驗（內容 4）；列舉、轉折與總結轉承清楚（組織 4）；句子正確，有間接問句與現在完成式（文法句構 4）；用字正確但較平實（字彙拼字 3）。總分 15，屬穩健版。

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
In a corner of a shopping mall, a transparent vending machine has drawn a small crowd of teenagers. The poster on its side displays a series of twelve tiny animal figures, one of which is a “secret” edition hidden behind a large question mark. Standing in front of the machine, a boy stares at the figure he has just unwrapped, his face full of disappointment. Although seven or eight torn boxes already lie around his sneakers, the girl beside him is scanning a code on her phone to try her luck once more. On a nearby bench, meanwhile, two girls are happily trading their duplicates, turning bad luck into a small business deal. The scene captures both sides of the craze in a single frame: the excitement of the next box and the disappointment of the last.
The appeal of blind boxes lies in a clever mix of chance and collection. Since buyers never know which figure they will get, every box offers a moment of suspense similar to opening a gift, and that small thrill can be surprisingly addictive. On top of that, a complete set gives young people a clear goal, and showing off a rare figure on social media earns them attention among friends. For example, last year I spent almost two months of pocket money, roughly NT$3,000, chasing a single hidden panda, only to receive my ninth copy of the same rabbit. Admittedly, the hobby is not entirely negative; trading duplicates helped me make friends with collectors from other schools. Still, its long-term effects deserve attention. To begin with, students who keep buying “just one more” on impulse can easily lose control of their spending, much like lottery players hoping that the next ticket will win. In addition, every figure comes with a box, a plastic bag, and a paper card that are thrown away within seconds, so the hobby leaves behind a surprising amount of trash. In the end, I have come to see self-control as the real “secret edition”: setting a monthly budget and buying only the figures I truly love can keep a fun hobby from turning into an expensive habit.

steady.comment_zh: 第一段由販售機海報（十二款、隱藏版問號）寫到失望的男生與空盒、準備再買的女生、交換公仔的兩人，要點齊全；第二段兩個受歡迎的原因、一週零用錢買五盒沒抽到熊貓的經驗、金錢與垃圾兩項影響，最後提出設預算的看法。全文無語言錯誤，not knowing what is inside 語序正確；字彙（secret figure、pocket money、budget）準確但偏基本，For example 接在 I understand this feeling well 後稍突兀。

top.comment_zh: 第一段細節完整並以 both sides of the craze 收束；第二段先以 chance and collection 解釋受歡迎的原因（懸念、成套目標、社群炫耀），用花 NT$3,000 只抽到第九隻兔子的經驗佐證，讓步承認交到朋友，再寫衝動消費與垃圾兩項影響，最後以 self-control 是真正的隱藏版收尾，呼應巧妙。句型與字彙（suspense、addictive、duplicates、on impulse）精準，無語言錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段涵蓋販售機、海報、隱藏版、失望的男生與空盒、準備再買的女生、交換公仔的兩人；第二段有兩個受歡迎的原因、兩項影響（花費、垃圾），並用自己花一週零用錢買了五盒的經驗支持，最後提出設預算。文法與拼字都正確；字彙貼切（secret figure、collect a whole set、budget、trade）。three hundred dollars 沒有寫 NT$，在台灣情境下略不精確（E2 有寫 NT$）。

top.comment_zh: 第一段以 turning bad luck into a small business deal 與「一幅畫面看見兩面」收束，圖中每個重點都寫到；第二段原因（懸念、收集成套、社群炫耀）、經驗（NT$3,000、第九隻兔子）、交友的好處、金錢與垃圾的壞處，最後以 self-control 為 secret edition 回扣。句型豐富，用字精準，沒有錯誤。
